Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — benchmark FrontierRefactor (60 performance-oriented refactoring tasks, four contract scales Kernel/Module/Package/Repository, in-place optimization and cross-language rewriting, seven source languages) with a reference-free cascaded protocol (compliance, functional equivalence, noise-calibrated speedup); six model + harness configurations, 3 trials each (1,080 runs); trajectory analysis; multi-turn feedback experiment

No SDD approach. Agents compared: Claude Code v2.1.278 (Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Fable 5, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), Codex CLI v0.155.1 (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol), all at high reasoning effort. Multi-turn feedback variants (GPT-6 Astra): Blind Retry, Scalar Speedup, Noise-Aware Timing

Benchmark task (Harbor v0.18 package): task.toml (metadata), instruction.md (standardized task specification given to the agent: task facts, workspace layout, contract and equivalence protocol, constraints and anti-circumvention rules), environment/ (baseline code), tests/ (held-out probes and workloads). Observable contract: caller-visible interface plus allowed dependencies and prohibited symbols

Agent receives code base and contract only, produces a refactored candidate; evaluation in three cascaded gates: compliance (static AST audit, container isolation) -> functional equivalence (frozen differential probes, zero partial credit) -> performance (worst-case speedup over workloads above calibrated noise floor). RQ5 adds up to three feedback rounds

60 tasks x 3 trials. Criterion per submission: strict success = all three gates (benchmark's authoritative criterion); no configuration-level success threshold stated by the authors. Pass@1 / strict@3 / best-of-3 / functional pass / avg speedup / conversion / Overall Score avg@3 / steps / tokens (M) / cost ($) (Table 3): (a) Claude Code v2.1.278 + Claude Opus 5: 34.4% / 16.7% / 51.7% / 78.9% / 1.13x / 43.7% / 0.84 / 48.9 / 8.02 / $18.57; (b) Claude Code + Claude Sonnet 5: 26.1% / 13.3% / 38.3% / 57.2% / 1.11x / 45.6% / 0.71 / 26.3 / 4.28 / $1.55; (c) Claude Code + Claude Fable 5: 26.1% / 6.7% / 46.7% / 64.4% / 1.13x / 40.5% / 0.74 / 23.9 / 4.77 / $0.61; (d) Codex CLI v0.155.1 + GPT-6 Astra: 30.6% / 16.7% / 41.7% / 79.4% / 1.09x / 38.5% / 0.86 / 20.5 / 1.55 / $2.11; (e) Codex CLI + GPT-5.6 Sol: 25.6% / 13.3% / 41.7% / 70.0% / 1.08x / 36.5% / 0.80 / 29.3 / 2.67 / $1.36; (f) Claude Code + DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: 40.0% / 31.7% / 50.0% / 80.0% / 1.15x / 50.0% / 0.86 / 115.8 / 20.65 / $0.50. Quality and cost verdicts: no criterion stated by the authors. RQ5 (GPT-6 Astra, 25 tasks, strict success round 1 -> 3): Blind Retry 16.0% -> 32.0%; Scalar Speedup 16.0% -> 40.0%; Noise-Aware Timing 16.0% -> 28.0% (avg speedup 1.05x, highest relative gain). Reference points: non-agent baselines 0.0%, human expert solutions 100.0% strict success, 1.84x mean speedup

Tasks: 60 FrontierRefactor tasks. Configurations: 6 model + vendor-native harness pairs at high reasoning effort; DeepSeek run under Claude Code for a controlled comparison within one harness. Baseline: original code (speedup reference), non-agent baselines and human expert references. Held constant: instruction.md as sole prompt (no bespoke prompts), containers without network, pinned shallow clones, 8 dedicated CPU cores and 32 GB RAM, timing protocol. Agent harness differs across vendors (not held constant). Acceptance tests: held-out differential probes and workloads. Repetitions: 3 independent trials per task. Human intervention: none. Ablations: reasoning effort (4 levels, 25 tasks, Opus 5 and GPT-6 Astra); multi-turn feedback (3 arms, 3 rounds, 25 tasks); gate removal counterfactuals

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + Claude Code best on Pass@1 (40.0%) and strict@3 (31.7%) at lowest cost ($0.50); Claude Opus 5 best on best-of-3 (51.7%) and Overall Score best-of-3 (0.93) at highest cost ($18.57). Across systems 41.2% of runs (445) pass functionality but fail to accelerate (19.3% slower, 21.9% noise-bound); conversion 42.5% of 774 functionally passing. Cross-language 43.1% strict success vs in-place 17.8%; cross-language functional pass drops from 65.0% (module) to 32.6% (package). Repeated benchmark cycles associated with +21.1 pp strict success (p < 1e-4, observational). Reasoning effort: no monotonic gain (p = 0.48 Opus 5, 0.83 Astra). Scalar feedback 16.0% -> 40.0% (McNemar p = 0.031). No significance tests between the six configurations

Distinguished configurations and exposed correctness-speed decoupling; 0/50 empirical false positives under null calibration (95% CI 0.0-5.8%); compliance gate never triggered in primary runs but intercepted 31 circumvention attempts; counterfactuals show +33.5/+34.2 pp inflation without compliance gate. Repeatability: 3 trials, strict@3 shows large drop from best-of-3 (agents accelerate stochastically). No limitations of the method stated by the authors

No limitations section. Gaps stated: refactoring benchmarks check correctness only, performance benchmarks are single-scale micro-kernels; raw timing without noise calibration is unreliable; agents lack profiling and noise-tolerant self-validation; future agents need active profiling tools and hardware telemetry
